concepts.name: Schedules of WPA 1972: Classification and Protection Levels
key_dimensions: Original 6 Schedules vs. post-2022 amendment consolidation into 4 Schedules (I, II, III, IV)
Schedule I species: absolute protection, highest penalties, no exceptions even for research
Difference in penalty structure across schedules and the UPSC trap of which schedule offers 'maximum' protection
Vermin category (Schedule V) and its implications for culling — species like Common Crow, Fruit Bats, Rats, Mice

concepts.name: 2022 Amendment to WPA 1972: Structural and Substantive Changes
key_dimensions: Reduction of schedules from 6 to 4 and renumbering implications
Insertion of provisions to implement CITES obligations domestically — new chapter on regulation of trade in scheduled specimens
Strengthening of penalties: minimum imprisonment increased, fines revised upward
Introduction of 'Management Authority' and 'Scientific Authority' under CITES framework within the Act

concepts.name: Protected Areas Network: National Parks vs. Wildlife Sanctuaries
key_dimensions: Key distinction: human activities (grazing, collection of forest produce) permitted in Sanctuaries but NOT in National Parks
Boundary alteration: National Park boundaries can only be altered by State Legislature resolution (not executive order) — a classic UPSC trap
Wildlife Sanctuary boundaries can be altered by the State Government — no legislative requirement
Overlap with Forest Rights Act 2006 and settlement of rights before declaring National Parks

concepts.name: Conservation Reserves and Community Reserves: Concept and Distinction
key_dimensions: Added by 2002 amendment to create buffer/corridor zones — Conservation Reserves on government land, Community Reserves on community/private land
Community Reserve: only category under WPA where local communities have formal co-management role via Community Reserve Management Committee
Conservation Reserve Management Committee appointed by State Government — composition and powers
UPSC trap: Community Reserves can be declared on private land unlike National Parks or Sanctuaries which require government land

concepts.name: Tiger Reserves under Project Tiger and WPA 1972 Interface
key_dimensions: Tiger Reserves have no independent statutory basis in WPA 1972 — they are notified under the Wild Life (Protection) Act through the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) framework inserted by 2006 amendment
Core/Critical Tiger Habitat vs. Buffer Zone — legal basis under Section 38V
Relocation of communities from Core zones: voluntary vs. mandatory provisions and Supreme Court rulings
NTCA composition: chaired by Minister of Environment, Vice-Chair is Minister of State — distinction from other statutory bodies

concepts.name: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA): Statutory Powers and Accountability
key_dimensions: Established under Section 38L by 2006 amendment — statutory body, NOT a constitutional body
Powers: can de-notify Tiger Reserves only with concurrence of Tiger Conservation Authority of State and NTCA
Tiger Conservation Plan: mandatory for each reserve — contents and legal enforceability
NTCA annual report must be laid before Parliament — accountability mechanism

concepts.name: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB): Mandate and Jurisdiction
key_dimensions: Statutory body under WPA 1972 (Section 38Y inserted by 2006 amendment) — subordinate to Ministry of Environment
Functions: collect intelligence, coordinate with state agencies, compile data on wildlife crime — NOT a prosecuting agency
UPSC trap: WCCB does NOT have power of arrest independently; it coordinates with police and forest officials
Difference from TRAFFIC (international wildlife trade monitoring network) — TRAFFIC is an NGO, WCCB is statutory

concepts.name: Prohibition on Hunting: Scope, Exceptions, and Permit System
key_dimensions: 'Hunting' defined broadly under Section 2(16) — includes capturing, trapping, poisoning, destroying, and even disturbing eggs or nests
Exceptions to hunting ban: self-defense, disease/disability of animal (mercy killing), unavoidable killing — Chief Wildlife Warden permission required
Special permits for scientific research, education, snake venom extraction — Section 12 permits
UPSC trap: vermin (Schedule V species) can be hunted without permit — distinction from other schedules

concepts.name: Trade and Commerce in Wildlife: Sections 39–49 Provisions
key_dimensions: All wild animals, their body parts, trophies vest in the Government of India (Central Government) — not State Government
Declaration of trophies and animal articles: persons possessing prior to act must declare within prescribed time
Certificate of Ownership (COO): transferability rules — can be transferred only by inheritance or gift, NOT by sale for Schedule I and Part II of Schedule II species
CITES Appendix I species trade prohibition aligns with Schedule I of WPA — UPSC overlap question

concepts.name: Ivory Trade Regulation and Elephant-Specific Provisions
key_dimensions: 1991 amendment: banned commercial trade in ivory — complete prohibition on import/export of ivory
Antique ivory (pre-1972) exemption: requires registration with designated authority — a major enforcement loophole
Elephants are Schedule I animals but can be owned as 'captive elephants' — special provisions under Section 42
Distinction between wild elephant (WPA protection) and captive elephant (ownership rights of mahout/owner) — jurisdictional confusion

concepts.name: Chief Wildlife Warden: Powers, Functions, and Accountability
key_dimensions: Apex wildlife authority at state level — appointed by State Government under Section 4
Key exclusive powers: grant/refuse permits for scientific research, declare boundaries of sanctuaries (subject to collector's report), compound offences for minor violations
Cannot delegate certain powers — UPSC trap on which powers are non-delegable
Distinction from Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) — separate officer hierarchy in most states

concepts.name: Cognizable and Non-Cognizable Offences under WPA 1972
key_dimensions: Offences related to Schedule I and Schedule II Part II species are cognizable and non-bailable
Other offences may be non-cognizable — police can arrest without warrant only for cognizable offences
Compounding of offences: Chief Wildlife Warden can compound minor offences — acts as out-of-court settlement mechanism, reduces judicial burden
UPSC trap: Forest Officers below a certain rank CANNOT compound offences — only Chief Wildlife Warden or authorized officers

concepts.name: Invasive Species and Vermin Provisions: Schedule V
key_dimensions: State Government can declare any wild animal as 'vermin' for a specified area/period under Section 62
Declared vermin can be hunted without license — exception to general prohibition
Nilgai, Wild Pig declared vermin in certain states — political and ecological controversy
UPSC trap: declaration as vermin is TEMPORARY and AREA-SPECIFIC — not a permanent change in Schedule

concepts.name: Zoos and Captive Animals: Central Zoo Authority (CZA)
key_dimensions: CZA established under Section 38A by 1991 amendment — statutory body under Ministry of Environment
Functions: recognize, derecognize zoos; set minimum standards for upkeep; coordinate exchange of animals between zoos
UPSC trap: CZA does NOT control private ownership of wild animals — that is regulated separately under Section 42 (certificate of ownership)
No zoo can be established without prior approval of CZA — even government zoos require recognition

concepts.name: Forest Rights Act 2006 vs. WPA 1972: Conflict and Resolution
key_dimensions: FRA 2006 recognizes rights of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers — but WPA 1972 restricts activities in Protected Areas
Section 4(2) of FRA: rights cannot be recognized in Critical Wildlife Habitats unless rights are settled and communities relocated — sequencing requirement
Gram Sabha role in FRA vs. absence of community role in WPA 1972 Protected Area governance — democratic deficit argument
Supreme Court in Narmada Bachao, Wildlife First cases: balance between tribal rights and wildlife conservation — UPSC essay/GS angle

concepts.name: Border Areas and Protected Area Governance: Special Provisions
key_dimensions: Central Government can declare National Parks and Sanctuaries in Union Territories directly — States require Governor/State Government notification
For areas along international borders, Central Government has override powers — national security vs. conservation conflict
Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs): declared under Environment Protection Act 1986, NOT WPA 1972 — a critical UPSC distinction
Supreme Court's 10 km ESZ mandate around Protected Areas (T.N. Godavarman case) — legal basis and implementation challenges

concepts.name: CITES and WPA 1972: Domestic Implementation Mechanism
key_dimensions: India is a signatory to CITES (1976) — WPA 1972 serves as domestic implementing legislation
2022 amendment explicitly inserted provisions for CITES compliance: Management Authority (DGFT designated) and Scientific Authority (Wildlife Institute of India designated)
CITES Appendix I (ban on commercial trade) broadly corresponds to Schedule I of WPA — but not identical, creating enforcement gaps
Re-export certificates and CITES permits: which authority issues them in India — Management Authority, not Chief Wildlife Warden

concepts.name: Biosphere Reserves and WPA 1972: Exclusion and Overlap
key_dimensions: UPSC trap: Biosphere Reserves have NO statutory basis under WPA 1972 — they are UNESCO designations administered by MoEFCC through executive orders
A Biosphere Reserve may CONTAIN a National Park or Sanctuary within its core zone — but the legal protection comes from WPA, not BR designation
Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme: three-zone model (core, buffer, transition) vs. WPA's Core-Buffer demarcation in Tiger Reserves — conceptual confusion
Ramsar Sites, UNESCO World Heritage Sites also lack WPA statutory backing — governance entirely through executive action and international treaty obligations

concepts.name: Penalties, Offences, and Burden of Proof under WPA 1972
key_dimensions: Reverse burden of proof: accused must prove innocence regarding possession of scheduled animal articles — Section 50 presumption
Enhanced penalties for repeat offences — second conviction for Schedule I offences carries enhanced minimum sentence
Officers empowered to search without warrant in certain circumstances — Section 50 powers of entry, search, seizure and arrest
UPSC trap: Penalty for damaging a National Park (without hunting) is different from penalty for hunting — two separate offence categories

concepts.name: Migratory Species and WPA 1972 Limitations
key_dimensions: WPA 1972 protects species within Indian territory — does NOT extend to high seas or foreign territories, creating gaps for migratory species like Olive Ridley Turtles
Convention on Migratory Species (CMS/Bonn Convention): India is a signatory — domestic compliance requires executive action, not automatic WPA protection
Great Indian Bustard, Amur Falcon: migratory species with partial WPA Schedule I protection but international coordination required for effective conservation
Marine Protected Areas: declared under WPA 1972 (e.g., Gulf of Mannar) but enforcement jurisdiction overlaps with Coastal Regulation Zone and Maritime laws — institutional fragmentation
